ai.description: This frog measures 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct cream-colored, V-shaped marking on the snout and prominent, fleshy, disk-like tips on its fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus athirappillyensis* is best distinguished by its unique, prominent, and pointed snout, which is significantly more elongated than that of other night frogs.
ai.habitat: The Athirappilly Night Frog inhabits riparian zones within evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 100 and 300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Athirappilly Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus athirappillyensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices or near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus athirappillyensis* is endemic to the Vazhachal forest region in Kerala’s southern Western Ghats, occurring at elevations between 300 and 500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Athirappilly Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "ticking" calls, typically heard from rocky stream banks within its dense forest habitat.
